title: Ada and the Safehouse
premise: Yara Lockridge, a fixer-interpreter for delegations that governments prefer to disown, is handed a routine job translating for a failing peace summit in a border city. Mid-flight, the delegation's aircraft vanishes from every record — manifests, radar archives, even the memories of the officials who booked it — and Yara realizes the erasure is the work of the Safehouse, a deniable training network she was unknowingly groomed by years ago. To survive the week, she must trace her own buried inheritance inside the Safehouse, turn its graduates against it, and burn the network's archive before the border checkpoint changes shifts at dawn. She succeeds, but at the cost of her old name, her handler's life, and the certainty that she was ever anything but what they made her.
about_author: Freya Nakamura is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent a decade working summits across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about the people who speak for others and the institutions that decide who gets heard.

chapters.title: The Language of Small Doors
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She takes a last-minute contract interpreting for a fragile peace delegation in the border city of Veren, sensing the job is a setup no one will claim. She notices her credentials were approved too easily. Emotional beat: professional unease disguised as routine competence.

chapters.title: Delegation of One
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the pre-summit dinner, she interprets a threat hidden inside diplomatic pleasantries and realizes one delegate is speaking a coded dialect she shouldn't recognize — but does. Emotional beat: the first crack in her belief that her past is behind her.

chapters.title: Flight 44
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with an interlude from air-traffic controller Mateo Reyes. The delegation's aircraft drops from every record while still airborne; Mateo remembers a plane that no system will confirm. Emotional beat: vertigo — the world editing itself in real time.

chapters.title: What the Manifest Forgot
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She pulls the paper backup of the flight manifest and finds her own name on a passenger list for a trip she never took. Her handler, Ilse, goes silent mid-call. Emotional beat: dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Safehouse Doctrine
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, a decade earlier. A young Yara is trained in a safehouse: languages, deniability, how to disappear a person politely. Emotional beat: tenderness curdling into the revelation that Yara was an asset, not a student.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Veren
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She tries to leave the city and is waved through a checkpoint by a guard who greets her by a name she hasn't used in years. Emotional beat: the trap has no walls, only doors that open too readily.

chapters.title: Graduates
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She tracks down Tomas, a fellow graduate now working border security, and confronts him with the vanished flight. He admits the Safehouse is being retired — and its graduates with it. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance, fear shared like contraband.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Ear
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He shows Yara how the erasure was executed: a linguistic key embedded in the delegation's own translation channels, including hers. Emotional beat: guilt — she may have carried the weapon herself.

chapters.title: Ilse's Last Transmission
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A dead-drop message from Ilse gives her a location and a warning: the archive burns at shift change or not at all. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude braided together, and the first clear goal.

chapters.title: The Summit That Never Was
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The peace talks collapse on schedule, exactly as designed, and the delegates begin vanishing into the same recordless silence as Flight 44. Emotional beat: fury at the machinery of plausible deniability.

chapters.title: Names We Buried
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, with flashbacks in Ilse's voice. She decodes Ilse's message using a childhood cipher only the two of them shared, learning the archive's location beneath the old safehouse. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed — not money, but method and debt.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Nothing
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV: Director Voss, the Safehouse's architect, reviews Yara's file and orders her 'reabsorbed.' Emotional beat: cold administrative menace; Yara is a line item, not a threat — yet.

chapters.title: Reabsorption
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She is ambushed by a graduate she once trusted, escapes by turning the Safehouse's own tradecraft against her attacker. Emotional beat: survival at the price of becoming, briefly, exactly what they trained.

chapters.title: Tomas Breaks
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Interrogated by Voss's people, Tomas holds out just long enough to misdirect them toward the wrong border crossing. Emotional beat: courage measured in minutes bought.

chapters.title: Twelve Hours to Shift Change
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She assembles her plan: recruit three wavering graduates, forge a checkpoint rotation, and reach the safehouse before dawn. Emotional beat: the thriller engine at full burn — a heist against her own makers.

chapters.title: The Choir of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The recruited graduates gather in a shuttered church; old loyalties fracture, and one betrays the meeting's location to Voss. Emotional beat: fragile solidarity, then the sick drop of betrayal.

chapters.title: Voss Offers Her a Name
chapters.summary: Yara and Voss meet face to face; he offers her the directorship and her original identity restored. Emotional beat: temptation — the chance to be someone again, if she becomes the network's next mask.

chapters.title: The Archive Below
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She infiltrates the safehouse's sublevel, where every erased flight, delegate, and interpreter lives in analog records the digital purge missed. Emotional beat: awe and horror at the scale of the ledger.

chapters.title: What Burns, What Stays
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She begins destroying the archive but keeps one file: the truth of Flight 44, to be delivered to the one journalist still listening. Emotional beat: choosing witness over erasure — the theme's hinge.

chapters.title: Checkpoint, Shift Change
chapters.summary: Yara's POV and Tomas's, converging. The graduates seize the checkpoint rotation for exactly eleven minutes; Voss's forces converge; Ilse arrives, alive, and takes a bullet meant for Yara. Emotional beat: the climax's chaos and sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Border Moves
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The checkpoint shifts, the archive is ash, Voss is erased by his own system — a recordless man at last. Yara crosses with the Flight 44 file in a language no one at the checkpoint can read. Emotional beat: exhausted triumph, grief for Ilse.

chapters.title: Yara, Interpreting
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, weeks later. The Flight 44 story breaks; the delegation's survivors are named back into existence. Yara takes a new name and a small honest job, keeping only Ilse's cipher as inheritance. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — identity as something chosen, not assigned.
